findings.title: Numeric IPv4 notation bypasses the metadata block
findings.problem: InstanceConfig(url="http://2852039166", enabled=True) passes the new validator. In web/validation.py:150-171, this hostname misses BLOCKED_HOSTS and ipaddress.ip_address raises ValueError, so it is accepted as DNS. Verified locally that HTTPX preserves this host and socket.getaddrinfo with AI_NUMERICHOST resolves it to 169.254.169.254 without DNS. startup.py:155 passes the accepted URL to ArrClient, whose connection check sends a request to that metadata address.
findings.why_it_matters: This defeats the metadata restriction this change explicitly introduces.
findings.fix_hint: Normalize or reject alternate numeric IPv4 representations before the hostname fallback, then apply the blocked-address checks. Add a regression test rejecting http://2852039166 while preserving supported loopback URLs.

members.title: SSRF validator bypassed by alternate numeric IP notation (decimal/hex/octal)
members.problem: validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:153-171) decides whether a hostname is a blocked IP literal solely via ipaddress.ip_address(hostname). That raises ValueError (treated as an accepted DNS name) for hostnames in decimal, hex, or dotted-octal integer form, even though the OS resolver used by httpx (triggarr/clients/base.py:29-30) resolves those strings straight to the literal IP. Verified: ipaddress.ip_address('2852039166'), ('0xa9fea9fe') and ('0251.0376.0251.0376') all raise ValueError so validate_arr_url_config returns (True, ''), while socket.getaddrinfo on each resolves to 169.254.169.254, the cloud-metadata address the docstring says is blocked. The pre-existing validate_arr_url has the same flaw.
members.why_it_matters: A URL such as http://2852039166/latest/meta-data/ passes validation and httpx resolves it to 169.254.169.254 at request time, enabling SSRF to the cloud metadata service, exactly the outcome the new validator claims to prevent.
members.fix_hint: In validate_arr_url_config/validate_arr_url, do not rely on ipaddress.ip_address() to decide whether a hostname is an IP literal; pre-normalize with socket.inet_aton-equivalent parsing or reject purely numeric/hex/octal hostnames outright, then apply the blocked checks.
members.current_code:
ok, err = validate_arr_url_config(v)
        if not ok:
            raise ValueError(err)
        return v

members.title: Config-load SSRF check bypassed by trailing-dot FQDN and integer-form IPv4 hosts
members.problem: The new validator delegates to validate_arr_url_config. That function matches hosts against BLOCKED_HOSTS by exact string (validation.py:150) and parses IP literals only with ipaddress.ip_address (validation.py:154). 'http://metadata.google.internal./' returns (True, '') because the trailing-dot FQDN is not in the set. 'http://2852039166/' also returns (True, '') because ip_address raises ValueError on a decimal integer string and the except branch passes it as a hostname. httpx.URL keeps the host unchanged, and glibc getaddrinfo/inet_aton resolves those forms to 169.254.169.254. So the cloud-metadata targets this validator says it blocks still load from triggarr.toml.
members.why_it_matters: Metadata-endpoint SSRF that the docstring promises to block at config load is still reachable with trivially encoded hosts.
members.fix_hint: in validate_arr_url_config, rstrip('.') the hostname before the BLOCKED_HOSTS lookup, and reject all-numeric/hex single-label hosts (or normalize them with socket.inet_aton) before the ip_address check

members.title: URL rejected at startup now crashes with an uncaught ValidationError traceback
members.problem: The validator runs on every instance, including disabled ones, so an existing triggarr.toml that loaded before now fails Settings construction. Examples are a schemeless 'radarr:7878' or '192.168.1.5:7878', which return (False, 'URL scheme must be http or https'). ensure_config (triggarr/config.py:370-373) catches only TOMLDecodeError/UnicodeDecodeError and lets pydantic.ValidationError propagate as a 'schema bug'. A user-data validation failure therefore becomes a raw traceback out of asyncio.run, not the friendly loguru error and exit(1). The traceback goes to stderr outside the redacting loguru sink and includes pydantic's input_value, which is the full URL and may contain userinfo credentials.
members.why_it_matters: Upgrading turns a previously tolerated disabled-instance URL into a crash-loop with an unredacted traceback, and the cause is not obvious to the operator.
members.fix_hint: catch pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config, log a sanitized field-path + message via loguru (no input_value), and sys.exit(1)

members.title: ValidationError text now includes rejected URLs (possibly with userinfo credentials) in logs and startup tracebacks for more inputs
members.problem: Pydantic v2 ValidationError str() includes input_value. Before this diff only URLs with an apikey= query parameter raised from the url field. Now any non-http, link-local, metadata or unspecified URL raises too, so a URL like 'http://user:pass@169.254.1.1' would appear in routes.py:599 logger.warning('Invalid settings rejected: {exc}'), in routes.py:794, and in the uncaught startup traceback on stderr outside the loguru redacting sink. The redacting sink scrubs known API key values, not URL userinfo.
members.why_it_matters: Credentials in reverse-proxy URLs could leak into container logs.
members.fix_hint: Where ValidationError is logged or surfaced, log exc.errors(include_input=False) or a summary of field locations plus messages instead of str(exc).
